streams.title: Individual Crop Production
streams.subtitle: For independent farmers and landholders managing agricultural land in Gujarat
streams.description: Comprehensive third-party inspection and certification for individual agricultural landholders seeking organic status under the National Standards for Organic Production (NSOP). Covers cereals, pulses, oilseeds, spices, cash crops, and horticulture.
streams.transitionPeriod: 24 to 36 months (2 years for annual crops, 3 years for perennial orchards)
keyRequirements: Submission of application package and Indian Organic Standards compliance undertaking
100% of offer fees paid in advance by DD/cheque/online mode in favour of M/s. GOPCA payable at Ahmedabad
Daily maintained Farm Diary and on-farm input preparation records
3-meter buffer zones and physical isolation against conventional farmlands
Mandatory annual pre-harvest inspection, report preparation, and blind laboratory residue testing
streams.turnaroundTime: Intimated within 1 month after report & payment receipt

streams.title: Grower Groups (Internal Control System - ICS)
streams.subtitle: Cost-effective group certification for small and marginal farmer collectives
streams.description: Designed specifically for Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), cooperative societies, and village clusters where smallholders cultivate similar crops in geographical proximity under a unified Internal Quality System (IQS). Meets NPOP Section 5 criteria.
streams.transitionPeriod: 24 to 36 months (Farms of 4 hectares or more must be inspected annually; total area must be <50% of group)
keyRequirements: Registered legal entity (cooperative, FPO, registered society) with an organisational chart
Documented Internal Control System (ICS) manual and appointed Internal Quality Manager
100% internal inspections completed by ICS staff prior to external audit
External sampling by GOPCA under NPOP Section 5.5.12 based on √Total Farmers formula
Group certificate issued in the name of the group, not individual farmers
streams.advanceRequirement: 75% advance payment before inspection, 25% balance on final clearance

streams.title: Processing, Milling & Handling Facilities
streams.subtitle: Certified spice cleaning, oil extraction, cold storage, and packaging facilities
streams.description: Auditing and certification of post-harvest processing facilities, spice grinding mills, oil expellers, sorting-grading units, and packaging facilities ensuring complete physical segregation from conventional ingredients.
streams.transitionPeriod: Immediate once facility SOPs, pest control, and physical segregation are verified
keyRequirements: Documented organic integrity maintenance procedures and physical segregation
Traceability records matching input raw material with output packaged goods
Non-chemical pest management protocols inside storage and processing bays
Label artwork approval submitted to GOPCA prior to market distribution

streams.title: Commercial Organic Input Approval
streams.subtitle: Verification of commercial bio-fertilizers, bio-pesticides, and soil conditioners
streams.description: Third-party assessment of commercial agricultural inputs intended for organic agriculture to guarantee zero prohibited synthetic components, heavy metals, or GMO derivatives under NPOP Appendix 1.
keyRequirements: Complete ingredient disclosure and sourcing verification
Laboratory toxicology, heavy metal analysis, and bio-efficacy reports
Manufacturing site inspection and formulation quality control verification
Product labeling compliance with NPOP commercial input guidelines

faqs.question: What is Organic Certification?
faqs.answer: Organic certification is a certification process for producers of organic food and other organic agricultural products. Businesses directly involved in food production may be certified, including seed suppliers, farmers, food processors, retailers and restaurants. "Certified Organic" assures products were produced and/or processed under conditions required by National Standards and/or international standards for Organic Production.

faqs.question: Does GOPCA guarantee 100% absolute zero-residue or product quality?
faqs.answer: The homepage clarifies that organic certification is not a declaration of product quality, food safety or an absolute residue-free guarantee, and does not guarantee the efficiency of agricultural inputs. It is an impartial verification process to determine whether products claimed to be organic comply with NPOP organic certification standards and verified production practices.

faqs.question: What is the required conversion period before organic certification?
faqs.answer: As per NPOP guidelines, the conversion period is three years for perennial crops and two years for annual crops. Even where prior organic management is claimed, a mandatory minimum conversion of one year is required under the National Standards.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility for Grower Group (ICS) Certification?
faqs.answer: Producer groups must meet NPOP Section 5 criteria, including similar production systems, geographical proximity, legal status/constitution and an organisational chart. Farms of 4 hectares or more may be included but must be inspected annually by GOPCA; their total area must be less than 50% of the total group area.

faqs.question: How are fees paid for individual and group certification?
faqs.answer: For individual farmers, 100% of the offer fees are to be paid in advance by DD/cheque/online mode in favour of M/s. GOPCA payable at Ahmedabad. For Grower Groups (ICS), a 75% advance payment is required with the application, and the balance is settled upon final inspection and report completion.

faqs.question: How long is the certificate valid and how is it renewed?
faqs.answer: Certificate validity is one year and annual inspection is required. Renewal application and advance payment must be submitted in advance. Failure to renew within the stipulated time can close the operator file and require immediate cessation of GOPCA logo use.

faqs.question: Does GOPCA certify produce for direct export?
faqs.answer: As per current official scope, GOPCA offers certification primarily for the domestic market under NPOP standards, and export certification services may be expanded in the future. Operators are guided to APEDA NPOP export equivalency pathways where applicable.
